jobs.prompt:
Add a runnable verify command (bun run check) so CI can verify changes

Context: https://github.com/ubiquity/xp.ubq.fi/issues/8 reports that this repository has no CI workflow running on `pull_request` and no runnable verify command (a `test` or `check` script). This task delivers the verify command and makes it pass. Use bun for everything (see .clinerules); do not use node or npm.

Current state on `development` (reproduce it first with `bun install`, `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun test`):
- package.json has no `test` or `check` script, and `type-check` runs `tsc --noEmit --watch`, which never exits.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` reports about 33 errors, in src/ (for example `'items' is of type 'unknown'` in src/utils/data-transformer.ts), in tests/ (missing `bun:test` imports), and in tools/build-assets.ts, which is a Deno script (`jsr:` imports, `Deno` global) that the bun tsconfig wrongly includes.
- `bun test` fails: tests/download-artifacts.test.ts imports `downloadAndStoreArtifacts` from src/download-artifacts.ts, which no longer exports it, and tests/final-artifact-e2e.test.ts calls the live GitHub API and throws unless GITHUB_OWNER, GITHUB_REPO and GITHUB_TOKEN are set.

What to change:
1. package.json scripts: make `type-check` a one-shot `tsc --noEmit`; move the watching variant to a new `type-check:watch` and point `dev:frontend` at it so that script keeps its behavior; add `test` (`bun test`); add `check`, which runs type-check, then test, then build, and exits non-zero if any of them fails.
2. Make `bun run type-check` exit 0 by fixing the real type errors with correct types. Do not use `any` casts, `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error`, or looser compiler options to silence them. Files that are Deno-only (tools/build-assets.ts, deno/, worker/ if they fail for that reason) may be excluded from tsconfig.json, since tsc with bun-types cannot check them; exclude nothing else.
3. Make `bun test` exit 0 with no network access and no environment variables. Rewrite tests/download-artifacts.test.ts against what src/download-artifacts.ts actually exports today, keeping it a meaningful test of the download-and-store flow with mocked I/O; do not delete it or reduce it to a trivial assertion. Make tests/final-artifact-e2e.test.ts skip itself (bun's `test.skipIf` or equivalent) when GITHUB_OWNER, GITHUB_REPO or GITHUB_TOKEN is missing, run unchanged when they are set, and import `test` and `expect` from `bun:test`.
4. tools/build.ts swallows failures with `.catch(console.error)`; make a failed build exit non-zero so `check` can detect it.
5. Add a short "Verifying changes" section to README.md naming `bun run check`.

Constraints:
- Do not create or modify any file under `.github/workflows/`. The token that publishes your branch cannot push workflow files, and the push would be rejected. Instead, end your final message with a section titled "Proposed CI workflow" containing, in one fenced yaml block, the complete contents of a `.github/workflows/ci.yml` that a maintainer can add by hand: triggers `pull_request` and `push` to `development`, `permissions: contents: read`, one job on `ubuntu-latest` that checks out the code, sets up bun with `oven-sh/setup-bun@v2`, runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile` and then `bun run check`. It must use no secrets.
- Do not change runtime behavior of the app, the deploy workflow, wrangler.toml, or dependency versions beyond what the steps above need. If bun.lock changes, the change must come from `bun install` only.
- Follow .clinerules (kebab-case file names, no CSS in TypeScript or HTML).

Done when, from a fresh clone with no .env file and no GITHUB_* variables set, `bun install --frozen-lockfile && bun run check` exits 0, and `bun run check` exits non-zero if you temporarily introduce a type error or a failing test (verify both, then revert). State the commands you ran and their results in your final message, before the "Proposed CI workflow" section.
